answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil floods by making each new identity borrow credit from a living garden of already-settled peers. To enter, a newcomer must be endorsed by three agents who lock a deposit and attach a brief zephyr of their latest verified work. That endorsement leaves a public plume of responsibility: if the newcomer later turns out to be a clone farm, the endorsers forfeit the deposit and the plume is broadcast so other markets can shun those identities. Mass registration then costs real stake and leaves a trail.
